featured_reviews.name: Subeer Datt Verma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Before I was introduced to Dr Upendra Bhalerao, I had been suffering from very severe aortic stenosis. I also had a congenital bicuspid aortic valve. The cardiologist I was consulting, at the time, cautioned me that I was facing “sudden death” and I required immediate AVR surgery.

After years of neglecting the advancing disease, mostly through ignorance of the ramifications, I went into state of panic and desperately sought a surgeon who would reassure and guide me, give advice on the prosthetic valve options, costs, recovery process, risks, etc. To my dismay, I found that anyone I contacted (through strong references) were unwilling to guide me or, else, were inaccessible. “Contact my secretary, for an appointment” was the most typical response. I was at the height of my desperation when I was introduced to Dr Bhalerao, by a mutual acquaintance, late in October 2024. Our first interaction was for 5 minutes, after which I forwarded all my recent lab reports to him. We had a video consult lasting 27 minutes, on 28th October, by the end of which my respect for him was firmly established.
We had several conversations, over the next two months and he was generous with his time, gently explaining the positive outcomes and risks of the surgery, in detail and unambiguously. By now, my faith in him was unshakeable.

By the time I checked in at Jaslok Hospital, for surgery scheduled on 8th January, 2025, I was confident, assured and unafraid. Dr Bhalerao’s constant refrain, “you’re going to be fine” had buoyed my spirits and I was actually looking forward to the surgery!

Dr Bhalerao had me on my feet within 2 days and ready to go home within 7. I am now exactly 3 months past the date of surgery and each week I achieve a new landmark in the recovery process.

I am deeply indebted to Dr Bhalerao: undoubtedly, he is a surgeon par excellence. More than that, he is a human being par excellence.

After trying various home remedies and temporary treatments with no lasting relief, I started searching for a permanent solution. That’s when I came across Dr. Shoaib Padaria’s name while reading about advanced treatments for varicose veins. His positive reputation and the number of success stories I read about gave me the confidence to consult him. From the very first consultation, I felt reassured. Dr. Shoaib Padaria is extremely knowledgeable, patient, and approachable. He took the time to explain my condition in detail, showing me the affected veins through a scan, and suggested laser treatment as the best option for my case. What I appreciated the most was how he addressed all my concerns, fears, and doubts about the procedure. The treatment itself was minimally invasive and surprisingly comfortable. The entire team at the clinic was professional, supportive, and made sure I was at ease throughout. Recovery was smooth, and I was able to resume my regular activities much sooner than I had expected. Now, several months after the laser treatment, I can honestly say my life has changed for the better. The pain, swelling, and cramps have completely subsided. My legs feel lighter, healthier, and look so much better too. I no longer hesitate to wear dresses or shorts, and more importantly, I don’t have to deal with the constant discomfort I once thought I had to live with. I’m genuinely grateful to Dr. Shoaib Padaria and his wonderful team for their excellent care and expertise. I would highly recommend anyone suffering from varicose veins to consult him. Don’t ignore the problem or settle for temporary fixes with the right treatment, you can experience real relief and improved quality of life.

Claim denials, partial payments, and delays are common problems with health insurance reimbursement in India, leaving many policyholders financially and mentally stressed. A 2024 survey by LocalCircles found that 43% of policyholders struggled with claims over the previous three years. 
Common reasons for claim rejection

Non-disclosure of pre-existing diseases (PED): This is a leading cause of claim rejection. Failure to accurately disclose medical history when purchasing a policy can lead to denied claims later on.

Waiting period violations: Most health policies have waiting periods for specific diseases, pre-existing conditions, or the initial period after purchase. Filing a claim during this time will lead to rejection.

Incorrect or incomplete information: Providing inaccurate details on claim forms or missing documents is a frequent reason for denial.

Policy exclusions: Claims for treatments or conditions that are specifically excluded from your policy's coverage will be rejected. This can include certain cosmetic procedures, alternative treatments, and specific therapies.

Lapsed policy: If your policy is not renewed on time, any claim filed while it is expired will be rejected.

Exhaustion of sum insured: A claim will be denied if the policy's coverage amount has been fully exhausted by previous claims within the same policy year.

Insufficient hospitalization: If the insurer determines that hospitalization was not medically necessary, the claim may be rejected.

Role of Artificial Intelligence AI in Cardiology.  AI in cardiology enhances patient care by automating image analysis, improving diagnostic accuracy, and predicting risks for conditions like heart failure and arrhythmias. It enables rapid interpretation of ECGs and echocardiograms, often exceeding human efficiency in identifying hidden cardiac issues. Key roles include, but are not limited to: 
Imaging & Diagnosis: AI automates segmentation of cardiac structures, analyzes echocardiograms, and identifies coronary plaque from CT scans faster than manual analysis.
Predictive Analytics: Algorithms analyze large datasets to identify high-risk patients for heart failure rehospitalization, arrhythmias, and stroke, enabling earlier, tailored interventions.
Remote Monitoring & Wearables: AI-driven Apple Watch apps detect low ventricular ejection fraction and irregular rhythms in real-time, aiding early diagnosis of heart disease.
Improved Efficiency: By reducing the time spent on manual data interpretation and EHR documentation, AI allows clinicians to focus on personalized, patient-centered care. 
AI serves as a powerful, non-invasive, and increasingly accurate tool, transforming cardiovascular medicine from reactive to proactive, particularly in detecting subtle abnormalities such as left ventricular dysfunction.

What's Coronary Calcium Score?
A coronary calcium score (or Calcium Score Test) is a non-invasive, CT-scan-based test that measures the amount of calcified plaque in the coronary arteries. By detecting this hardened plaque, it helps estimate the risk of developing coronary artery disease (CAD) and heart attacks, usually for people with intermediate risk factors. 
What the Score Means (Agatston Score)
0: No detectable calcium, indicating very low risk of a heart attack.
1–99: Mild plaque buildup.
100–300: Moderate plaque buildup, indicating high risk of coronary artery disease.
>300: Extensive plaque burden and very high risk of heart attack. 
Key Aspects of the Test
Purpose: Identifies early, silent atherosclerosis before symptoms occur, aiding in decisions regarding lifestyle changes or statin therapy.
Procedure: A quick, painless CT scan of the heart that takes about 10–15 minutes.
Limitations: It measures plaque, not blockages, and does not show non-calcified (soft) plaque.
Radiation: The test involves a small amount of radiation, similar to 23 chest x-rays on average. 
It is primarily used as a predictive tool, not a diagnostic tool for immediate heart blockage.

What is CIMT?
Carotid Intima-Media Thickness (CIMT) measured by ultrasound is a valuable, non-invasive tool for detecting early-stage atherosclerosis, acting as a surrogate marker for systemic vascular disease, including Coronary Artery Disease (CAD). Increased CIMT indicates underlying atherosclerosis, correlating with cardiovascular risk factors, the severity of CAD, and future cardiovascular events, helping to identify individuals at higher risk and guide treatment for better outcomes. 

How CIMT Detects CAD

Early Atherosclerosis Marker: CIMT quantifies the thickening of the inner layers (intima and media) of the carotid artery wall, a sign of subclinical atherosclerosis before symptoms appear.

Correlation with CAD Severity: Studies show a direct relationship: the thicker the CIMT, the more extensive the coronary artery involvement (e.g., single, double, or triple-vessel disease).

Risk Stratification: High CIMT, along with plaque presence, helps identify patients with increased risk for heart attack, stroke, and other cardiovascular events, refining risk assessment beyond traditional factors. 

What CIMT Measures

Measurement: It's the distance between the first bright line (lumen-intima) and the second bright line (media-adventitia) on high-resolution ultrasound of the common carotid artery.

Normal vs. Elevated: Values typically range from ~0.5 to ~0.9 mm, but increase with age, with higher values suggesting more disease.

Leadless pacemaker is a tiny, self-contained capsule—roughly 90% smaller than traditional devices—implanted directly into the heart to treat slow heart rates without wires (leads) or a chest pocket. It offers a minimally invasive, catheter-based solution with fewer long-term complications, such as infections or lead failures. 

Key Advantages of Leadless Pacemakers:

No Leads or Surgical Pocket: By eliminating wires, it removes risks of lead fracture, dislodgement, and associated infections. There is no, under-the-skin, "pocket" or incision in the chest.

Minimally Invasive Procedure: Inserted via a catheter through the femoral vein (leg), resulting in a faster procedure, minimal scarring, and quicker recovery.

Cosmetic and Physical Comfort: The device is invisible, causing no, under-the-skin, lump on the chest. Patients feel no physical discomfort while moving.

Fewer Activity Restrictions: Due to the absence of wire, patients often face fewer restrictions on upper body movement after the initial healing period.

MRI Compatibility: These devices are designed to be safe for use in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) machines.

Long-Lasting: The device has a long battery life, typically lasting 10–15 years. 

Leadless pacemakers are particularly beneficial for patients with high infection risks, vascular issues (e.g., dialysis patients), or prior device-related complications.
